mem.t: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

lessons.title: The Word God Breathed Out
lessons.theme: Scripture is God’s word, the standard for life

v: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
For no prophecy ever came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

lessons.still: Hold your Bible in both hands and be still for a moment. Tell the Lord, “This is your word, not human opinion.” Ask the Holy Spirit to help you open this book today with reverence and longing.
teach: If a map were drawn by someone who had never been to the place, we would not dare to trust it on a mountain trail. But if it were drawn by the very one who made the mountains, we could follow it with confidence. The Bible is that kind of map: not human guesses about God, but God’s revelation to humanity.

The word “inspired” literally means “God-breathed.” Just as God breathed into Adam and he became a living being, God moved people by his Spirit to write the Scriptures, and so this book carries God’s own breath. Peter says prophecy never came from the will of man; rather, people spoke from God as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. That is why Scripture is profitable for us in four ways: teaching, reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness.

Our mindset shapes how we read the Bible. If we treat it as a reference book, we will read only the parts we like; if we treat it as God’s word, we will let it examine us. The purpose of reading Scripture is not to make us people with lots of knowledge, but “that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: One of the three foundations—Scripture is my standard. It is not I who judge Scripture, but Scripture that judges me. Laying down my own opinions and returning to my place as a learner is letting Jesus reign in the realm of truth.
q: Who is God? — What kind of God is willing to “speak” and to put his heart into writing?
Who am I? — Do you more often let Scripture “examine you,” or do you “pick and choose” from Scripture?
How shall I respond? — How will you show today that Scripture has the final authority in your life?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was tempted, three times he answered, “It is written.” He was the Son of God, yet he gladly took Scripture as his standard; he also said, “The Scripture can’t be broken.” If the Lord himself honoured Scripture this way, how much more should we take it as the standard for our lives.
lessons.pray: God who speaks, thank you that you did not leave us groping in the dark, but wrote your heart down for us in the Scriptures. Give me a reverent heart to receive your word without picking and choosing and without watering it down. Holy Spirit, use your word to teach me, reprove me and correct me, so that I may be complete. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: On the inside cover of your Bible, write: “This is God’s word, my standard”
Before reading Scripture today, pray: “Lord, please speak to me through your word”
lessons.noon: “Every Scripture is God-breathed.” — Lord, right now I am willing to be shaped by your word.

lessons.title: Read, Reflect, Pray, Do
lessons.theme: Four steps that bring God’s word into our lives

v: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
but his delight is in the LORD’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.

lessons.still: Choose the short passage you will read today, but don’t rush into it. Take a deep breath and tell the Lord, “I haven’t come to finish my homework; I’ve come to meet you.” Then read it slowly the first time, as you would read a letter from home sent from far away.
teach: You can’t eat a meal by just reading the menu, nor by bolting it down whole. You put it in your mouth, chew it slowly, swallow and digest it, and finally it becomes strength for your work. Reading Scripture is the same: reading is putting it in your mouth, reflecting is chewing, praying is digesting and absorbing, and doing is turning it into strength. Skip any step and you lose part of the nourishment.

Joshua 1:8 itself contains clear steps: “shall not depart from your mouth”—read; “meditate on it day and night”—reflect; “observe to do”—do. Psalm 1 says such a person is like a tree planted by streams of water. The word “meditate” originally carries the sense of murmuring something over and over in a low voice—like a cow chewing the cud, turning the word over and over until it becomes your prayer.

In practice: Read—read a short passage slowly and circle the words that touch you. Reflect—ask, “What does this passage show me about God? About myself?” Pray—turn that sentence into a prayer, responding to God. Do—set one concrete small action for today. This is exactly the daily flow of this app.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Changing our mindset takes eight steps, from Information and Revelation to Conviction and Practice. The four steps of Bible reading walk this very road: reading is Information, reflecting seeks Revelation, praying is Conviction, and doing is Practice. A changed mindset changes our life, and a changed life changes how we live.
q: Who is God? — God promises “good success”; what kind of relationship is that promise built on?
Who am I? — Of the four steps—read, reflect, pray, do—which do you most often skip?
How shall I respond? — Which passage will you read today using the four steps?
lessons.jesus: Jesus’ life was a life saturated with Scripture. Tempted in the wilderness, he quoted Deuteronomy readily; on the cross he still prayed the Psalms. God’s word was not only on his lips but in his heart and in his actions. He is the one who read, reflected, prayed and did most perfectly.
lessons.pray: Lord, I don’t want to just look at the menu and never eat the bread of life. Teach me to meditate on your word day and night, letting it pass from my mouth into my heart, become my prayer, and then turn into my actions. Make me like a tree planted by streams of water, bearing fruit in its season. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Read Psalm 1 using the four steps, and write down one action for today
Say a verse that touched you today three times, like chewing the cud
Rewrite a verse as your own prayer
lessons.noon: “This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night.” — Lord, right now I chew on your word again.

lessons.title: Meeting the Lord in Scripture
lessons.theme: We read Scripture to come to Jesus and receive life

v: “You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify about me.
Yet you will not come to me, that you may have life.
They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”

lessons.still: Imagine you are one of the disciples on the road to Emmaus, walking along in disappointment and confusion, when a stranger comes alongside you. Say quietly, “Lord, please open the Scriptures to me yourself today, and set my heart on fire.”
teach: If someone read every biography of a famous person but never met or spoke with them, they would only “know about” that person; they would not truly “know” them. Bible reading can be like that: more and more knowledge, but a heart growing colder and colder—even turning proud and using verses to measure others.

Jesus said to religious leaders who knew the Scriptures well: You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life, yet they testify about me, and you will not come to me to have life. The problem was not that they hadn’t read enough, but that after reading they would not “come.” The disciples on the road to Emmaus were the opposite: as the Lord opened the Scriptures to them, their hearts burned within them.

So as we read, we should keep asking, “What kind of Jesus does this passage show me?” The Bible is like a road, and its destination is Jesus himself. Our mindset needs to shift from “How many chapters must I finish?” to “Whom will I meet today?” The amount is not the point; the meeting is.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Jesus is my example; Scripture is my standard; the Holy Spirit is my guide—and all three meet in Bible reading: the Holy Spirit opens the Scriptures so that I see Jesus. Knowledge that puffs us up becomes mere decoration for the self-ruled life; a real encounter makes us humble and on fire.
q: Who is God? — Jesus drew near to his discouraged disciples; what does this show you about his heart?
Who am I? — When you read the Bible, is your heart more cold or on fire? Why?
How shall I respond? — After reading today, with what words will you respond to the Lord you have met?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus walked a long road with two discouraged disciples, and beginning from Moses and all the prophets he explained to them what the Scriptures said about himself. The whole Bible is his self-introduction. Even now, by the Holy Spirit, he opens our minds so that we meet him in the Scriptures.
lessons.pray: Risen Lord, I don’t want merely to know things about you without knowing you. As you did on the road to Emmaus, open the Scriptures to me yourself, open my mind, and set my heart on fire. Every time I open the Bible, let me come to you and receive life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: After reading today, write: “The Jesus I saw today is…”
Let go of the pressure of a reading plan; read just a short passage and chew on it slowly
Share with a friend a verse that set your heart on fire
lessons.noon: “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way?” — Lord, right now please speak to me again.

lessons.title: After Looking in the Mirror
lessons.theme: Hearing and doing the word builds our life on the rock

v: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;
for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.
“Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.

lessons.still: Recall a verse you read yesterday and quietly ask yourself, “Did I do it?” Don’t rush to defend yourself or to blame yourself; simply see it honestly before the Lord, and then say, “Lord, today I am willing to do it.”
teach: Imagine looking in the mirror in the morning, seeing a smudge on your face, then turning away, forgetting all about it, and going out with the smudge all day. It sounds absurd. Yet James says that is exactly what people are like who hear the word and don’t do it: they see themselves in the mirror of Scripture, yet nothing changes.

James calls this “deluding your own selves”—thinking that knowing is the same as doing. Jesus told of two men building houses. Both heard his words, and on an ordinary day their houses looked much the same; the difference only showed when the storm came. One “does them,” and his house is built on the rock; the other does not, and his house is built on sand.

Obedience is not gritting our teeth with willpower; it is the obedience that responds to grace. Start small: each time you read, set just one action you can do today; in the evening review it, reflect and correct, then repeat the next day. Truth only truly becomes ours when we live it out.
lessons.light: 321 Light: In the eight steps of changing our mindset, Conviction is followed by Practice, Review, Correction and Repetition. Knowing without doing stops at “Information”; when we live it out, our mindset becomes life, and life becomes the way we live. Letting Jesus reign means letting his word have the final say in me.
q: Who is God? — When God gives us the mirror of Scripture, is it to condemn us or to heal us?
Who am I? — Which truth have you long “known” but still not put into practice?
How shall I respond? — Which word you already know will you put into practice right away today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work.” For him, obeying the Father’s word was not a burden but nourishment. From the manger to the cross, his whole life was God’s word put into practice.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often hear and then forget; I know a great deal but do very little. Forgive me for deceiving myself. Today I want to build my life on the rock of your word—not only hearing it, but doing it. Holy Spirit, give me the strength to obey. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose a verse you have long known but not yet practised, and live it out today
In the evening, take three minutes to review: Did I do what I read today?
Tell a spiritual companion about today’s practice and ask them to check in with you
lessons.noon: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man.” — Lord, right now I am willing to obey.

lessons.title: A Lamp to My Feet
lessons.theme: God’s word lights up today’s next step

v: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
The entrance of your words gives light. It gives understanding to the simple.

lessons.still: Imagine walking a mountain path at night with only a small lamp in your hand, lighting up just a step or two ahead. Quietly tell the Lord, “I don’t need to see the whole journey; I only ask you to light up my next step today.”
teach: The oil lamps of ancient times were not very bright; they lit only a short stretch of path just ahead. The psalmist says God’s word is “a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path”—not a floodlight on the blueprint of the next ten years, but light for how to walk today. We often want to see the whole route clearly before we set out, but God invites us to follow the light one step at a time.

“The entrance of your words gives light. It gives understanding to the simple.” The light does not come from our cleverness but from God’s word being opened up—like drawing back the curtains so the light pours in. So we read Scripture with a humble heart, admitting that we are “the simple” who need light. The proud, who think they see clearly, end up seeing nothing.

This week we have seen that Scripture is the God-breathed standard; that we read it through four steps—read, reflect, pray, do; that the purpose of reading is to meet Jesus; and that obeying matters more than knowing. Today we hide God’s word in our hearts and let it shine at every fork in the road. Next week we will learn to respond to this speaking God through the Lord’s Prayer, which Jesus himself taught.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard. Our perspective shifts—from the human point of view to God’s, from the temporary to the eternal. Letting God’s word be a lamp to our feet means letting Jesus reign in every choice, building what belongs to God step by step.
q: Who is God? — God is willing to lead us “step by step”; what does this show you about his patience?
Who am I? — Do you often hesitate to take the next step because you can’t see the whole road?
How shall I respond? — Which choice you face today needs the light of God’s word?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.” God’s word is a lamp because it points to the true Light. Those who follow Jesus don’t need to see the whole road first; they only need to follow the light closely.
lessons.pray: Lord, your word is a lamp to my feet and a light for my path. I don’t ask to see the whole road; I only ask you to light up my next step today. Open up your words and give understanding to someone as simple as me; and help me to hide your word in my heart and follow you at every fork in the road. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down a decision you are facing, and find a related verse
At the weekend, share with a spiritual companion one ray of light you received from Scripture this week
lessons.noon: “Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.” — Lord, right now please light up my next step.
